source_text: Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἠξιώθην ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ Δαμᾶ τοῦ ἀξιοθέου ὑμῶν ἐπισκόπου καὶ πρεσβυτέρων ἀξϊων Βάσσου καὶ Ἀπολλωνίου καὶ τοῦ συνδούλου μου διακόνου Ζωτίωνος, οὗ ἐγὼ ὀναίμην, ὅτι ὑποτάσσεται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὡς χάριτι θεοῦ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς νόμῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
thought_title: Worthy to see the Magnesians through their bishop and clergy
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the church in Magnesia, has just spoken of his chains and his prayer for unity, and now tells them how he came to see them through their leaders.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore I was deemed worthy to see you through Damas your bishop worthy of God and the worthy elders Bassus and Apollonius and my fellow servant the deacon Zotion, of whom I may have joy, because he is subject to the bishop as to the grace of God and to the council of elders as to the law of Jesus Christ.

choices.why: The compound adjective describes the bishop as one who bears God's worth; rendering it as a phrase keeps the force of the Greek compound without inventing a hyphenated English compound.
The term marks shared servitude to Christ; 'fellow slave' preserves the literal force of σύν + δοῦλος and Ignatius's humility in placing himself alongside the deacon.
The optative expresses a wish; 'may I have joy of' keeps the optative force and the sense of deriving benefit or delight from someone.
rejected: would that I might benefit from

choices.why: The middle voice indicates willing submission; 'he is subject' preserves the present tense and the ongoing posture of obedience.

choices.english: as to the grace of God
choices.why: The ὡς clause expresses the manner or ground of submission; 'as to' keeps the comparative force without flattening it into mere equivalence.

choices.english: as to the law of Jesus Christ
choices.why: Parallel to the preceding clause; 'as to the law' preserves the pairing of grace and law that structures Ignatius's thought.
rejected: as if to the law of Jesus Christ

pass_b_english: So I was counted worthy to see you in the persons of Damas your bishop, who is worthy of God, of your worthy elders Bassus and Apollonius, and of my fellow slave Zotion the deacon. May I have joy of Zotion, for he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the council of elders as to the law of Jesus Christ.

edits.old: of my fellow slave Zotion the deacon
edits.new: of my fellow servant Zotion the deacon

fixed: Standardized syndoulos to 'fellow servant' in both English and gloss, since the brief's glossary does not specify a term but the confirmed problem notes inconsistency; 'fellow servant' is the more common rendering and avoids the harsher connotation of 'slave'.

The 'council of elders' vs 'elders' issue is not a real problem in this section: the source uses πρεσβυτέρων for the individuals (Bassus and Apollonius) and πρεσβυτερίῳ for the council, so the English correctly distinguishes the persons from the body.
